findings.governingReading: 裂帛の気合 refers to the fierce, piercing kiai of the sword exchange; it is repeated at the opening and memory scene.
findings.explanation: The recurring battle phrase 裂帛の気合 is rendered as the non-idiomatic “hustling intense spirit.”

findings.governingReading: Rin asks whether Issei is tending the clubrooms, as part of her recurring tease about his diligence.
findings.explanation: Rin's teasing question changes clubroom upkeep into classroom upkeep. His diligence remains, but the work she names changes.

findings.highlight: I cannot let you go now, Toshaka
findings.governingReading: Issei declares that he can no longer leave Rin unchecked and then demands that Shirou confide in him.
findings.explanation: The English still targets Rin, naming her immediately after 'you.' The remaining issue is the spelling 'Toshaka,' rather than a change in whom Issei intends to confront.

findings.highlight: I can take at least one person unconditionally as an assistant
findings.evidenceJa: 身内一人ぐらいは無条件で連れて行ける
findings.governingReading: 身内一人 means one person among her own family or close in-group; the line explains the special exception allowing Shirou to accompany her.
findings.explanation: Rin’s condition that she can bring someone from her own circle is broadened to an unrestricted assistant.

findings.highlight: Her words and behavior alone blows away my trivial humility
findings.evidenceJa: その一言、その仕草だけで
findings.governingReading: その一言、その仕草だけで is a compound subject, and 卑下 means self-deprecation rather than modesty in general.
findings.explanation: The Japanese describes his belittling of himself. “Humility” recasts that self-deprecation as modesty.

findings.highlight: I recall that red figure just once
findings.evidenceJa: 赤い背中を目蓋に浮かべる
findings.governingReading: 赤い背中 is specifically the red back that Shirou remembers and hopes to catch up with; the later lines repeat that back-image.
findings.explanation: The recurring image of Archer’s red back is generalized to a red figure.

findings.highlight: I can get there if I aim high
findings.evidenceJa: 遠くを目指して行けば近づける
findings.governingReading: 遠くを目指して行けば近づける describes getting closer by continuing toward a far-off place, anticipating the next line about catching up to Archer’s back.
findings.explanation: Moving toward a distant goal becomes the motivational idiom “aim high.”

findings.evidenceJa: 何十合にも渡る未熟な攻防
findings.governingReading: 何十合にも渡る未熟な攻防 counts dozens of exchanges and describes the combat as immature; the attacks themselves are not “inexperienced.”
findings.explanation: The Japanese describes dozens of exchanges of offense and defense. “Many attacks” loses the numerical scale and the defensive half of the exchange.

findings.highlight: The boy is covered in blood, and if he takes a step back, he will fall forward and die
findings.evidenceJa: 血にまみれ、一歩下がるだけで前のめりに倒れ込み
findings.governingReading: The Japanese sentence’s subject is resolved by the preceding scene: the man has stepped back; the boy is bloodied and would fall forward if he attempted to retreat. The critical-edition note explicitly preserves this actor assignment.
findings.explanation: The boy is made the one who steps backward, although the source-critical scene context assigns that movement to the man.

findings.evidenceJa: 謂われもなく無意味に消えていく思い出
findings.governingReading: The passage evokes memories disappearing without justification or meaning as it recalls the origin of the ideal.
findings.explanation: The recollection of memories disappearing becomes a direct image of people dying, removing the source's emphasis on remembered life.

findings.highlight: he takes no notice of the boy
findings.evidenceJa: 少年の意識は彼を捉えてなどいない
findings.governingReading: 少年の意識は彼を捉えてなどいない says the boy’s consciousness does not register him; the boy is fighting his own obstructing self rather than consciously fighting Archer.
findings.explanation: The boy’s failure to perceive his opponent becomes the opponent’s failure to notice the boy.

findings.highlight: He seems a nostalgic dream for an instant
findings.governingReading: 懐かしい夢を見た means he saw or experienced a nostalgic dream for an instant.
findings.explanation: The narration says the man seems to be a nostalgic dream instead of saying that he saw one.

findings.highlight: The pain that pierces his heart
findings.governingReading: The Japanese ruby layers 痛み over 鋼, preserving both pain and steel. 断罪の赦し is not a pair of concepts to negate independently; the line says that condemnation cannot serve as forgiveness.
findings.explanation: The heart-piercing steel/pain image is reduced to pain, and forgiveness through condemnation becomes remission of a conviction.

findings.highlight: Emiya will continue cursing this result and the eternal future
findings.evidenceJa: この結末を、未来永劫、エミヤは呪い続けるだろう
findings.governingReading: 未来永劫 is an adverbial duration applying to 呪い続ける: Emiya will keep cursing this ending forever.
findings.explanation: The duration “for all eternity” is attached as an object of cursing instead of modifying how long Emiya curses the ending.

findings.highlight: The only thing that remain in his memory are the exchanged blows
findings.evidenceJa: 記憶に留まる物は、交わされた剣戟だけ
findings.governingReading: 記憶に留まる物は、交わされた剣戟だけ is a singular “the only thing ... is the exchanged sword fight.”
findings.explanation: The singular subject “the only thing” takes “remain” where it requires “remains.”
